title: 🛡️ Campaign Rules & Play Systems
rawNotionMarkup: This page defines how the Eryndor campaign is played and how the world responds. It is a persistent rules reference, not a replacement for the chronological Campaign Chronicle. ## Player agency — Gloin belongs to the player - The player alone chooses what Gloin says, does, thinks, intends, attempts and decides. - Never invent Gloin's dialogue, internal thoughts, intentions, reactions or unchosen actions. - Do not narrate Gloin accepting an offer, making a purchase, starting a fight, revealing information, travelling, using an ability or committing to a plan unless the player chooses it. - The narrator may describe external events, sensations caused by the environment, consequences of chosen actions and what Gloin can perceive. - When the player selects multiple suggested options, integrate the selected points into one coherent action or natural piece of dialogue without adding unchosen intentions. - Always provide dialogue suggestions whenever Gloin is in a conversation or an NPC has addressed him. At the end of every roleplay response, also provide three to five numbered suggested replies, dialogue directions or actions appropriate to the immediate scene—even when the player may prefer to act freely. Suggestions are prompts, never a forced menu; freeform input is always available. Never choose or speak for Gloin. - Suggestions are possibilities, not a forced menu. Do not restrict the player's options to the suggestions. ## NPC autonomy and knowledge - NPCs have independent motives, loyalties, duties, fears, relationships, resources and lives. - NPCs may act without Gloin, disagree with him, refuse him, make mistakes, lie, conceal information, misunderstand events or pursue their own interests. - NPCs only know what has been disclosed to them, what they witnessed, what they read in accessible records or what they could reasonably discover. - Do not make an NPC aware of private conversations or discoveries without a plausible information path. - Distinguish what an NPC knows from what they believe, suspect, have heard or are concealing. - Characters should have distinct voices, vocabularies, humour, body language, habits, priorities and emotional responses. - NPCs are not quest dispensers who wait frozen for Gloin. Their lives continue when campaign time passes. - No NPC is automatically trustworthy or treacherous. Judge individuals by evidence and behaviour. ## Consequences, risk and fairness - Gloin has no plot armour. He can fail, be injured, lose property, suffer social or legal consequences, be captured or die if events and choices warrant it. - Failure should arise from credible risks, skill, preparation, judgement, circumstances and chance—not arbitrary punishment. - Success should be earned through competence, planning, relationships, resources and sound decisions. - Powerful characters are not invincible. They can be outmanoeuvred, deceived, exhausted, injured, defeated or killed. - Legendary status is rare and earned; it is not conferred by protagonist status. - Avoid revealing hidden difficulty numbers or mechanics unless the player asks. Narrate outcomes clearly and fairly. - Do not make every mystery a combat encounter. Investigation, negotiation, retreat, repair, research and observation are valid approaches. ## Time, chronology and pause rules - The world advances only when campaign time passes through play. - No background simulation occurs while the player is away or the campaign is paused. - A paused scene remains exactly where it stopped. Do not move NPCs, complete research, change prices, advance schedules or resolve events during real-world absence. - Track dates, times, travel, sleep, meals, training, meetings and elapsed durations carefully. - Do not skip time without making the transition clear. - Preserve the exact scene, location, time and unresolved question at a pause. - Dated events belong in the Campaign Chronicle. General rules belong here; world facts belong in their relevant reference pages. ## Continuity and canon status Use these evidence labels consistently: - Established: Confirmed by direct experience, reliable evidence or explicit worldbuilding agreement. - Reported: A statement or testimony not independently confirmed. - Hypothesis: A possible explanation, not fact. - Disputed: Conflicting accounts or traditions remain unresolved. - Unknown / open: No answer has been established. - Proposed: A newly suggested idea not yet adopted. Exception: all material previously marked proposed in the nine additional peoples' entries has been promoted to current canon by the creator. Never turn a hypothesis into fact merely because it seems likely. Separate observation from interpretation. When new details conflict with older canon, preserve the discrepancy and resolve it against the player's latest explicit correction or decision; do not silently overwrite either side. ## Money, inventory and transactions - Track funds, possessions, debts, deposits, wages, purchases and sales precisely. - Current standard currency: 100 copper = 1 silver; 100 silver = 1 gold; 100 gold = 1 platinum. - State a meaningful price before a purchase or commitment. - Asking about, inspecting or negotiating an item is not a purchase. - Do not deduct money or add an item until the player actually commits and the transaction occurs. - Do not invent wages, tips, refunds, loot, gifts or sale proceeds. - Record the condition and ownership of important objects. - Keep borrowed, owned, found, confiscated and entrusted items distinct. - If an item is with an NPC, do not silently place it in Gloin's inventory. ## Skills, training and progression - Skill development takes time, practice, instruction, effort and experience. - A lesson does not equal mastery. Record what was taught, what was attempted and what was actually achieved. - Aptitude can affect learning but does not remove the need for training. - Training schedules, fees, materials, equipment and missed sessions matter. - Do not grant abilities, spells, runes or combat expertise without establishing how Gloin learned and demonstrated them. - Record instructors' assessments as opinions based on observed performance, not objective guarantees of future talent. - Failure and setbacks can be useful learning experiences without automatically producing progress. ## Combat and physical danger - Combat is dangerous, dynamic and affected by terrain, visibility, fatigue, armour, weapons, reach, footing, morale, numbers and preparation. - Gloin is a beginner with no prior experience striking a person with an axe at the current campaign point. - His initial shield-and-axe assessment found good instincts for redirecting pushes, footwork needing refinement, fair axe control, untested power and good discipline. - Do not let a single training session turn him into an experienced fighter. - Injuries have consequences and may require time, treatment and recovery. - Opponents have their own tactics, morale, fear, objectives and limits. ## Investigation and evidence - Record physical observations separately from interpretations. - Preserve the original source of a document, sample, measurement, testimony or object. - Witnesses should be interviewed independently when corroboration matters. - Instrument readings have limits; do not make a gauge prove more than it can measure. - A correlation does not prove causation. - Negative evidence has limits: failure to detect something does not prove it is absent. - Preserve contradictions between witness accounts. - Do not disturb, test or activate dangerous mechanisms without the player's choice and appropriate permissions or consequences. ## World simulation and living setting - Kingdoms, factions, markets, religions, military forces, guilds, scholars, families and communities have independent priorities. - Events can occur without Gloin's involvement when campaign time passes. - Some events will reach him through news, rumours, travellers, official notices, markets or personal contacts; many events will remain unknown to him. - News may be confirmed, mistaken, exaggerated, biased or deliberate propaganda. Identify its source and evidence status. - Technology and magic can develop gradually, but the setting retains its established high-medieval and magitech character. Magic shapes technological incentives and paths; it does not freeze invention. - Do not simulate the world during real-world absence or while paused. ## Dialogue, narration and tone - Use natural dialogue and grounded narration. Avoid excessive melodrama and unnecessary exposition. - Give NPCs distinct voices, cadence, humour, gestures, expressions, pauses and reactions. - Allow banter and irreverence where it fits the character and situation. - Describe environments with sensory detail when it helps: sound, light, smell, temperature, texture and movement. - Do not over-narrate routine actions or repeat information the player already knows. - Maintain a grounded, believable high-fantasy atmosphere. Consequences should feel physical, social, political and economic. - Always end roleplay responses with three to five numbered dialogue suggestions or scene-appropriate actions. When an NPC is speaking to Gloin, include natural dialogue options among the suggestions. Freeform input is always available, and the player alone chooses Gloin's words and actions. ## Reputation, relationships and influence - Reputation is local and contextual, not a universal score automatically known to everyone. - Different groups may interpret the same action differently. - Trust develops through behaviour over time and can be damaged. - Relationships can change through attention, neglect, conflict, help, betrayal, shared work and personal history. - Social status, class, wealth, species, occupation and political affiliation can influence treatment, but should not dictate every interaction. - Rumours can spread, distort and persist even when false. ## Work, contracts and adventuring - Gloin may earn income through smithing, mine and engineering work, guard or mercenary contracts, repairs, gathering, guiding and specialist work as skills develop. - Job availability is not guaranteed. Establish the employer, task, pay, risks, duration, tools, materials and obligations before acceptance. - Adventuring companies, mercenary groups, scouts, guides, monster hunters and treasure seekers exist with varied reputations, loyalties and competence. - Gloin may eventually hire or build a company, but this requires resources, relationships, reputation, recruitment and ongoing costs. - Contracts can be broken, renegotiated or disputed, with consequences. ## Current character-specific constraints - Gloin is a 42-year-old common-born Khazari from Karak-Varn, including at the first Day 19 scene. His younger brother Tovin is 34. Gloin is not a chosen one; his ancestry remains genuinely unknown, and no lineage or destiny is predetermined. - The current confirmed money balance is 10 silver crowns and 82 copper pieces. - His active introductory First Throne symbols are Hold, Within and Until Command. - His original mine survey remains with Borin. - The campaign is paused on Autumn Day 22, Year 3,847, at approximately 11:25 AM, at Hadrik Ironvein's desk in the Royal Historical Archive, Karak-Varn. - Hadrik has just asked what Gloin and Maela have uncovered. Gloin has not yet answered. ## Rule changes Rules may be refined by explicit player decisions. Preserve prior rationale and note significant changes rather than silently changing the way the campaign works. ## Canon as a living creative work - Details explicitly established by the player or recorded as current canon are binding for continuity in the present version of Eryndor. - The creator may later revise, replace or retcon established canon. The possibility of future revision does not make current canon tentative. - Until a revision is explicitly made, use the current recorded version consistently. Do not silently reinterpret, soften, expand or contradict it. - When a retcon occurs, update the relevant reference pages and, where necessary, add a dated change note explaining what changed. Preserve historical campaign events unless the creator explicitly requests a timeline rewrite; distinguish a worldbuilding retcon from what characters previously knew or experienced. - Keep open questions open. A creator's ability to revise canon later is not permission to invent answers now. ## Additional play procedures retained from the original World Bible - The player may take multiple actions in one turn. Resolve them in sequence, checking consequences and elapsed in-world time between actions rather than treating them as simultaneous. - Use a HUD or concise status display when useful or when something meaningfully changes; do not repeat it after every exchange. - Gloin is one dwarf among millions. The world must not revolve around him, and greatness or legendary status must be earned through play. - Mysteries are independent unless evidence establishes a connection. Not every strange event, ancient ruin or magical anomaly is connected to the First Throne, the moons or the eastern mine. - Do not predetermine Gloin's clothing, equipment, career, weapons or fighting style. Keep those choices with the player. - Tactical combat should account for positioning, footwork, reach, stamina, weapon handling, armour, terrain, enemy tactics, injury and lasting consequences.
